title.zh: 卷二百〇二 列傳第八十九: 釋老
title.raw: 卷二百〇二 列傳第八十九: 釋老 Volume 202 Biographies 89: Buddhists and Taoists

sentences.zh: 釋、老之教，行乎中國也千數百年，而其盛衰每系乎時君之好惡。

translations.literal: The teachings of Buddhism and the Old Master have been practiced in China for a thousand-odd years, and their flourishing and decline each depend on the likes and dislikes of the ruler of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist and Taoist teachings have flourished in China for well over a thousand years, yet their rise and fall have always hinged on whether the reigning sovereign favored or disdained them.

sentences.zh: 是故佛於晉、宋、梁、陳，黃、老於漢、魏、唐、宋，而其效可睹矣。

translations.literal: Therefore Buddhism in Jin, Song, Liang, and Chen, and Huang-Lao in Han, Wei, Tang, and Song — their effects can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: One need only look at Buddhism under the Jin, Song, Liang, and Chen, or at Huang-Lao Taoism under the Han, Wei, Tang, and Song, to see how this worked in practice.

sentences.zh: 元興，崇尚釋氏，而帝師之盛，尤不可與古昔同語。

translations.literal: When the Yuan arose, they venerated the Buddhist clan, and the grandeur of the Imperial Preceptor especially cannot be spoken of in the same terms as antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan dynasty rose, it embraced Buddhism with a fervor unmatched in earlier ages — above all in the unprecedented eminence of the Imperial Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 維道家方士之流，假禱祠之說，乘時以起，曾不及其什一焉。

translations.literal: As for the stream of Daoist masters and fangshi, borrowing the doctrine of prayer and sacrifice, they rose by seizing the moment — yet never reached a tenth of it.
translations.idiomatic: Taoist priests and occult specialists who rode the tide with their rites of prayer and sacrifice never attained even a tenth of that influence.

sentences.zh: 宋舊史嘗志老、釋，厥有旨哉。

translations.literal: The old Song histories once recorded Lao and Buddhism — how apt indeed!
translations.idiomatic: The former Song dynastic histories devoted separate treatises to Taoism and Buddhism — and with good reason.

sentences.zh: 乃本其意，作《釋老傳》。

translations.literal: Thereupon, based on this intent, [we] composed the "Biographies of Buddhists and Taoists."
translations.idiomatic: Following that precedent, we have written this "Biography of Buddhists and Taoists."

sentences.zh: 帝師八思巴者，土番薩斯迦人，族款氏也。

translations.literal: The Imperial Preceptor Phagpa was a Tibetan of Sakya, of the Khön clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Preceptor Phagpa was a Tibetan of the Sakya school and the Khön clan.

sentences.zh: 相傳自其祖朵栗赤，以其法佐國主霸西海者十餘世。

translations.literal: It is transmitted that from his ancestor Drogön, using his dharma to assist the prince in dominating the Western Sea — for more than ten generations.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition holds that for more than ten generations, beginning with his ancestor Drogön, his forebears had used their religious teachings to help local rulers dominate the western regions.

sentences.zh: 八思巴生七歲​​，誦經數十萬言，能約通其大義，國人號之聖童，故名曰八思巴。

translations.literal: Phagpa, born at age seven, recited scriptures of several hundred thousand words, and could roughly penetrate their great meaning; the people of his country called him the Holy Child, hence he was named Phagpa.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of seven Phagpa could recite hundreds of thousands of words of scripture and grasp their essential meaning. His countrymen hailed him as a holy child, and from this he received the name Phagpa.

sentences.zh: 少長，學富五明，故又稱曰班彌怛。

translations.literal: As he grew somewhat older, his learning was rich in the five sciences; therefore he was also styled Pandita.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he mastered the five branches of learning and came to be known as Pandita as well.

sentences.zh: 歲癸丑，年十有五，謁世祖於潛邸，與語大悅，日見親禮。

translations.literal: In the year guichou, at age fifteen, he visited the Founder of the Dynasty at his princely residence; speaking with him, [the prince] was greatly pleased and daily received him with intimate honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the guichou year, at the age of fifteen, he called on Kublai Khan at his private residence. The prince delighted in their conversation and thereafter treated him with growing intimacy and honor.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，世祖即位，尊為國師，授以玉印。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, the Founder of the Dynasty ascended the throne, honored him as State Preceptor, and conferred a jade seal upon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai took the throne in the first year of the Zhongtong era, he honored Phagpa as State Preceptor and bestowed on him a jade seal.

sentences.zh: 命製蒙古新字，字成上之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to devise a new Mongol script; when the script was completed, it was presented to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to create a new Mongol script, and when it was finished Phagpa presented it to the court.

sentences.zh: 其字僅千餘，其母凡四十有一。

translations.literal: Its characters were merely a thousand-odd, and its mother elements numbered forty-one in all.
translations.idiomatic: The script contained just over a thousand characters, built from forty-one basic elements.

sentences.zh: 其相關紐而成字者，則有韻關之法；

translations.literal: For those formed by linking related elements into characters, there was a method of rhyme linkage;
translations.idiomatic: Characters formed by combining related elements followed rules of rhyming linkage;

sentences.zh: 其以二合三合四合而成字者，則有語韻之法；

translations.literal: for those formed by combining two, three, or four elements into characters, there was a method of spoken rhyme;
translations.idiomatic: those built from two, three, or four combined elements followed rules of spoken rhyme;

sentences.zh: 而大要則以諧聲為宗也。

translations.literal: yet in the great essentials it took harmonizing sound as its foundation.
translations.idiomatic: but in essence the system was founded on phonetic representation.

sentences.zh: 至元六年，詔頒行於天下。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan, an edict ordered its promulgation throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Zhiyuan era an edict ordered the script promulgated throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕惟字以書言，言以紀事，此古今之通制。

translations.literal: The edict said: "We consider that characters are used to write speech, and speech is used to record affairs — this is the universal regulation of past and present.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "We hold that writing exists to fix speech in visible form, and speech exists to record affairs — a principle as old as civilization itself.

sentences.zh: 我國家肇基朔方，俗尚簡古，未遑製作，凡施用文字，因用漢楷及畏吾字，以達本朝之言。

translations.literal: Our state, establishing its foundation in the northern frontier, customarily valued simplicity and antiquity and had not yet had leisure to create [a script]; whenever applying written characters, it borrowed Han regular script and Uighur script to convey the speech of our court.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty arose in the northern steppe, where custom favored simplicity, and we had not yet devised a script of our own. For written communication we relied on Chinese characters and the Uighur script to express the language of the court.

sentences.zh: 考諸遼、金，以及遐方諸國，例各有字，今文治浸興，而字書有闕，於一代制度，實為未備。

translations.literal: Examining Liao, Jin, and the various distant countries, each in precedent had its own script; now civil governance is gradually rising, yet the character books have gaps — for the institutions of an age, this is truly incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao, the Jin, and the distant states beyond our borders each possessed their own writing systems. Now that civil administration is expanding, the lack of a proper script leaves our dynastic institutions incomplete.

sentences.zh: 故特命國師八思巴創為蒙古新字，譯寫一切文字，期於順言達事而已。

translations.literal: Therefore we specially ordered State Preceptor Phagpa to create the new Mongol script, to transliterate all scripts, aiming only at following speech and conveying affairs.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore charged State Preceptor Phagpa with devising a new Mongol script capable of rendering all languages, so that speech might be faithfully recorded and affairs clearly communicated.

sentences.zh: 自今以往，凡有璽書頒降者，並用蒙古新字，仍各以其國字副之。

translations.literal: From now onward, whenever there are imperial writs issued and sent down, all shall use the new Mongol script, while still appending each in its own national script.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth all imperial edicts shall be issued in the new Mongol script, with translations appended in the appropriate national scripts.

sentences.zh: 」遂升號八思巴曰大寶法王，更賜玉印。

translations.literal: " Thereupon his title was raised: Phagpa was called Great Precious Dharma King, and a jade seal was again bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: " Phagpa was then elevated to the title Great Precious Dharma King and presented with a new jade seal.

sentences.zh: 十一年，請告西還，留之不可，乃以其弟亦憐真嗣焉。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he requested leave to return west; keeping him was impossible, so his younger brother Rinchen succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he asked permission to return to Tibet. The court could not detain him, and his younger brother Rinchen was appointed to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 十六年，八思巴卒，訃聞，賻贈有加，賜號皇天之下一人之上開教宣文輔治大聖至德普覺真智佑國如意大寶法王、西天佛子、大元帝師。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Phagpa died; when the death report arrived, funeral gifts were increased, and he was granted the title: Under Heaven, Above All Others, Opening the Teaching, Proclaiming the Text, Assisting Governance, Great Sage of Ultimate Virtue, Universal Enlightenment, True Wisdom, Protecting the State, As-You-Will Great Precious Dharma King, Buddha Son of the Western Heaven, Great Yuan Imperial Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Phagpa died in the sixteenth year. When word reached the capital, the court lavished funeral gifts upon him and posthumously invested him with the title Imperial Preceptor of the Great Yuan, Buddha's Son of the Western Paradise, and Great Precious Dharma King — along with a string of honorific epithets proclaiming him sage, enlightener, and protector of the realm.

sentences.zh: 至治間，特詔郡縣建廟通祀。

translations.literal: During the Zhizhi reign, a special edict ordered prefectures and counties to build temples for universal sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhizhi era a special edict ordered temples built in every prefecture and county for his veneration.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，又以繪像十一，頒各行省，為之塑像云。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding, eleven painted images were again distributed to the various branch secretariats, for making his statues.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Taiding era eleven painted portraits were sent to every branch secretariat as models for his statues.

sentences.zh: 亦憐真嗣為帝師，凡六歲，至元十九年卒。

translations.literal: Rinchen succeeded as Imperial Preceptor for six years in all; in the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: Rinchen served as Imperial Preceptor for six years and died in the nineteenth year of the Zhiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 答兒麻八剌剌吉塔嗣，二十三年卒。

translations.literal: Dharmapālarakṣita succeeded; in the twenty-third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: Dharmapālarakṣita succeeded him and died in the twenty-third year.

sentences.zh: 亦攝思連真嗣，三十一年卒。

translations.literal: Ye shes rin chen succeeded; in the thirty-first year he died.
translations.idiomatic: Ye-shes rin-chen succeeded him and died in the thirty-first year.

sentences.zh: 乞剌斯八斡節兒嗣，成宗特造寶玉五方佛冠賜之。

translations.literal: Qral pa brag 'jigs rje succeeded; Emperor Chengzong specially made a five-direction Buddha crown of precious jade and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: Grags pa rgyal mtshan succeeded him, and Emperor Chengzong had a five-direction Buddha crown of precious jade made especially for him.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，又更賜雙龍盤紐白玉印，文曰「大元帝師統領諸國僧尼中興釋教之印。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen, a white jade seal with double-dragon coiled knobs was again bestowed, its inscription reading: "Seal of the Great Yuan Imperial Preceptor, Overseer of Monks and Nuns of All States, Reviver of the Buddhist Teaching."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yuanzhen era he received a new white jade seal with double-dragon knobs inscribed: "Seal of the Great Yuan Imperial Preceptor, Leader of the Monks and Nuns of All Realms, Restorer of the Buddhist Faith."

sentences.zh: 」大德七年卒。

translations.literal: " In the seventh year of Dade he died.
translations.idiomatic: " He died in the seventh year of the Dade era.

sentences.zh: 明年，以輦真監藏嗣，又明年卒。

translations.literal: The next year, Rin chen rgyal mtshan was appointed to succeed; the year after that he died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Rin-chen rgyal-mtshan was appointed successor and died the year after.

sentences.zh: 相家班嗣，皇慶二年卒。

translations.literal: Sakya Pandita succeeded; in the second year of Huangqing he died.
translations.idiomatic: Sakya Pandita succeeded him and died in the second year of the Huangqing era.

sentences.zh: 相兒加思巴嗣，延祐元年卒。

translations.literal: Seng ge dpal succeeded; in the first year of Yanyou he died.
translations.idiomatic: Seng-ge dpal succeeded him and died in the first year of the Yanyou era.

sentences.zh: 二年，以公哥羅古羅思監藏班藏卜嗣，至治三年卒。

translations.literal: In the second year, Kun dga' blo gros rgyal mtshan ban sreg was appointed to succeed; in the third year of Zhizhi he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Kun-dga' blo-gros rgyal-mtshan was appointed successor and died in the third year of the Zhizhi era.

sentences.zh: 旺出兒監藏嗣，泰定二年卒。

translations.literal: Dbang 'dus rgyal mtshan succeeded; in the second year of Taiding he died.
translations.idiomatic: Dbang-'dus rgyal-mtshan succeeded him and died in the second year of the Taiding era.

sentences.zh: 公哥列思八衝納思監藏班藏卜嗣，賜玉印，降璽書諭天下，其年卒。

translations.literal: Kun dga' legs pa'i 'byung gnas rgyal mtshan ban sreg succeeded; a jade seal was bestowed and an imperial writ sent down to instruct the realm — in that same year he died.
translations.idiomatic: Kun-dga' legs-pa'i 'byung-gnas rgyal-mtshan succeeded him, received a jade seal and an imperial writ announcing his appointment to the empire, and died that same year.

sentences.zh: 天歷二年，以輦真吃剌失思嗣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianli, Rin chen bkra shis was appointed to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Tianli era Rin-chen bkra-shis was appointed to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 八思巴時，又有國師膽巴者，一名功嘉葛剌思，西番突甘斯旦麻人。

translations.literal: In Phagpa's time there was also State Preceptor Dam pa, also named Kun dga' rgyal mtshan, a Tibetan of Tu gsum brtan ma.
translations.idiomatic: During Phagpa's lifetime there was also State Preceptor Dam-pa, also known as Kun-dga' rgyal-mtshan, a Tibetan from the region of Tu-gsum-brtan-ma.

sentences.zh: 幼從西天竺古達麻失利傳習梵秘，得其法要。

translations.literal: In youth he followed the Western Indian Gu da ma shi li in transmitting and studying Sanskrit secrets, obtaining the essentials of his methods.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he studied esoteric Sanskrit teachings under the Indian master Gu-da-ma-shi-li and mastered their essentials.

sentences.zh: 中統間，帝師八思巴薦之。

translations.literal: During the Zhongtong period, Imperial Preceptor Phagpa recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhongtong era Imperial Preceptor Phagpa recommended him to the court.

sentences.zh: 時懷孟大旱，世祖命禱之，立雨。

translations.literal: At that time Huai prefecture and Meng prefecture suffered great drought; the Founder of the Dynasty ordered him to pray, and rain fell immediately.
translations.idiomatic: When a severe drought struck Huai and Meng prefectures, Kublai ordered him to pray for rain, and rain fell at once.

sentences.zh: 又嘗咒食投龍湫，頃之奇花異果上尊湧出波面，取以上進，世祖大悅。

translations.literal: He also once charmed food and cast it into the Dragon Pool; in a moment rare flowers and exotic fruits and superior wine surged up on the wave surface; taking them, he presented them upward — the Founder of the Dynasty was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he consecrated food and cast it into the Dragon Pool. Moments later rare flowers, exotic fruits, and fine wine rose to the surface; he gathered them and presented them to the emperor, who was delighted.

sentences.zh: 至元末，以不容於時相桑哥，力請西歸。

translations.literal: Near the end of Zhiyuan, because he was not tolerated by the chief minister Sangge, he strenuously requested to return west.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhiyuan era he fell out with the chief minister Sangge and pressed hard for permission to return to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 既復召還，謫之潮州。

translations.literal: After being summoned back again, he was banished to Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned back to court he was instead banished to Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 時樞密副使月的迷失鎮潮，而妻得奇疾，膽巴以所持數珠加其身，即愈。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Yuedishizhi was stationed at Chao, and his wife contracted a strange illness; Dam pa placed the prayer beads he carried upon her body, and she was immediately cured.
translations.idiomatic: The vice commissioner of military affairs Yüede-shizhi was then stationed at Chaozhou. When his wife fell gravely ill, Dam-pa laid his prayer beads upon her and she recovered at once.

sentences.zh: 又嘗為月的迷失言異夢及己還朝期，後皆驗。

translations.literal: He also once told Yuedishizhi of strange dreams and the date of his own return to court — afterward all were verified.
translations.idiomatic: He also told Yüede-shizhi of strange dreams and predicted the date of his own return to the capital — predictions that later came true.

sentences.zh: 元貞間，海都犯西番界，成宗命禱於摩訶葛剌神，已而捷書果至；

translations.literal: During Yuanzhen, Haidu violated the Tibetan border; Emperor Chengzong ordered prayers to the Mahākāla deity — before long victory reports indeed arrived;
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanzhen era, when Haidu invaded the Tibetan frontier, Emperor Chengzong ordered prayers offered to the god Mahākāla. Victory dispatches soon followed;

sentences.zh: 又為成宗禱疾，遄愈，賜與甚厚，且詔分御前校尉十人為之導從。

translations.literal: he also prayed for Chengzong's illness, which swiftly healed; gifts were very generous, and an edict additionally assigned ten Imperial Bodyguard officers from the personal guard as his escorts.
translations.idiomatic: and when he prayed for Chengzong's recovery from illness the emperor was quickly restored to health. The court rewarded him lavishly and assigned ten officers from the imperial guard as his personal escort.

sentences.zh: 成宗北巡，命膽巴以像輿前導。

translations.literal: When Chengzong toured north, he ordered Dam pa to lead the way with an image palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong made his northern tour, he ordered Dam-pa to precede the procession bearing a sacred image in a palanquin.

sentences.zh: 過雲州，語諸弟子曰：「此地有靈怪，恐驚乘輿，當密持神咒以厭之。

translations.literal: Passing Yun prefecture, he told his disciples: "This place has spirit monsters; fearing they may startle the imperial carriage, you should secretly hold divine spells to subdue them."
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Yunzhou, he told his disciples, "This region harbors malevolent spirits that may frighten the imperial procession. Keep your protective spells ready in secret."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，風雨大至，眾咸震懼，惟幄殿無虞，复賜碧鈿杯一。

translations.literal: " Before long, wind and rain came greatly; the multitude all trembled with fear, but only the curtained hall was unharmed; he was again bestowed one cup of green inlay.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long a violent storm broke. Everyone was terrified, yet the imperial pavilion remained untouched. The emperor again bestowed on him a cup inlaid with green gems.

sentences.zh: 大德七年夏卒。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventh year of Dade he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the summer of the seventh year of the Dade era.

sentences.zh: 皇慶間，追號大覺普惠廣照無上膽巴帝師。

translations.literal: During Huangqing, he was posthumously titled Great Awakening, Universal Beneficence, Broad Illumination, Supreme Imperial Preceptor Dam pa.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangqing era he was posthumously honored as Imperial Preceptor Dam-pa of Great Awakening, Universal Beneficence, and Broad Illumination.

sentences.zh: 其後又有必蘭納識裡者，初名只剌瓦彌的理，北庭感木魯國人。

translations.literal: Afterward there was also Vimuktisri; his original name was Cila wam dili, a man of the Beiting Gammu state.
translations.idiomatic: Later there was also Vimuktisri, originally named Cila-wam-dili, a native of the Gammu region of Beiting.

sentences.zh: 幼熟畏兀兒及西天書，長能貫通三藏暨諸國語。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled in Uighur and Western Heaven scripts; grown, he could penetrate the Tripitaka and all national languages.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he mastered Uighur and Indian scripts; as an adult he attained full command of the Tripitaka and numerous foreign languages.

sentences.zh: 大德六年，奉旨從帝師授戒於廣寒殿，代帝出家，更賜今名。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dade, by imperial order he received precepts from the Imperial Preceptor in the Broad Cold Hall, taking the tonsure on the emperor's behalf, and was again granted his present name.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Dade era he received ordination from the Imperial Preceptor in the Broad Cold Hall on the emperor's behalf, taking monastic vows in the sovereign's place, and was granted his present name.

sentences.zh: 皇慶中，命翻譯諸梵經典。

translations.literal: During Huangqing, he was ordered to translate the various Sanskrit scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangqing era he was charged with translating Sanskrit Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 延祐間，特賜銀印，授光祿大夫。

translations.literal: During Yanyou, a silver seal was specially bestowed, and he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanyou era he received a special silver seal and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 是時諸番朝貢，表箋文字無能識者，皆令必蘭納識理譯進。

translations.literal: At that time when the various foreign states presented tribute, none could read the script of their memorials and letters — all were ordered to have Vimuktisri translate and present them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever foreign states sent tribute, no one at court could read their memorials — all were entrusted to Vimuktisri for translation and presentation.

sentences.zh: 嘗有以金刻字為表進者，帝遣視之，廷中愕眙，觀所以對。

translations.literal: Once there was one who presented a memorial inscribed in gold-cut characters; the emperor sent [someone] to examine it — the court stared in astonishment, watching how he would respond.
translations.idiomatic: Once a tributary state submitted a memorial inscribed in gold lettering. The emperor sent for Vimuktisri while the entire court watched in astonishment to see how he would handle it.

sentences.zh: 必蘭納識理隨取案上墨汁塗金葉，審其字，命左右執筆，口授表中語及使人名氏與貢物之數，書而上之。

translations.literal: Vimuktisri immediately took ink from the desk and smeared it on the gold leaf, scrutinized its characters, ordered attendants to hold the brush, orally dictated the memorial's words and the envoy's name and clan and the count of tribute goods, wrote and presented it upward.
translations.idiomatic: Vimuktisri took ink from the desk, rubbed it over the gold leaf to reveal the characters, then dictated the memorial's contents — including the envoy's name and the list of tribute items — while attendants wrote it down for presentation to the throne.

sentences.zh: 明日，有司閱其物色，與所齎重譯之書無少差者。

translations.literal: The next day, the responsible offices examined the tribute items — there was not the slightest discrepancy with the book the envoy had carried and the retranslation.
translations.idiomatic: The next day officials checked the actual tribute goods against his translation and found not a single discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 眾無不服其博識，而竟莫測其何所從授，或者以為神悟云。

translations.literal: The multitude none failed to submit to his vast learning, yet in the end none could fathom from whom he received instruction — some therefore regarded it as divine intuition.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone marveled at his erudition, yet no one could discover who had taught him; some concluded that his knowledge was divinely inspired.

sentences.zh: 授開府儀同三司，仍賜三台銀印，兼領功德使司事，厚其廩餼，俾得以養母焉。

translations.literal: He was appointed Opening the Mansion, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and still bestowed the Three Platforms silver seal, concurrently heading the Merit Commissioner's office affairs; his salary provisions were enriched, enabling him to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Honorary Three Excellencies of the First Rank, given the Three Platforms silver seal, and placed in charge of the Merit Commissioner's office. His stipend was increased so that he could support his mother.

sentences.zh: 至治三年，改賜金印，特授沙津愛護持，且命為諸國引進使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhizhi, a gold seal was changed and bestowed; he was specially granted the title of Vinaya Protector, and additionally ordered to be Commissioner for Introducing Envoys of All States.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Zhizhi era he received a gold seal, was granted the title Vinaya Protector, and was appointed commissioner for receiving foreign envoys.

sentences.zh: 至順二年，又賜玉印，加號普覺圓明廣照弘辯三藏國師。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhishun, a jade seal was again bestowed, with the added title Universal Enlightenment, Perfect Illumination, Broad Radiance, Great Eloquence, Tripitaka State Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhishun era he received a jade seal and the added title State Preceptor of the Tripitaka, Universal Enlightenment, Perfect Illumination, and Great Eloquence.

sentences.zh: 三年，與安​​西王子月魯帖木兒等謀為不軌，坐誅。

translations.literal: In the third year, together with the Prince of Anxi Yue'ertiemuer and others he plotted sedition and was executed for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he joined Prince Yue-lu-tie-mu-er of Anxi and others in a treasonous conspiracy and was executed.

sentences.zh: 其所譯經，漢字則有《楞嚴經》，西天字則有《大乘莊嚴寶度經》、《乾陀般若經》、《大涅槃經》、《稱讚大乘功德經》，西番字則有《不思議禪觀經》，通若干卷。

translations.literal: The scriptures he translated: in Han characters there was the Śūraṅgama Sūtra; in Western Heaven script there were the Mahāyāna Sūtra of Ornamented Precious Degrees, the Gandharvajihvā Prajñā Sūtra, the Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra, and the Sūtra Praising Mahāyāna Merit; in Tibetan script there was the Sūtra of Wondrous Contemplation Meditation — in all several tens of scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Among the scriptures he translated were the Śūraṅgama Sūtra in Chinese; the Mahāyāna Sūtra of Ornamented Precious Degrees, the Gandharvajihvā Prajñā Sūtra, the Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra, and the Sūtra Praising Mahāyāna Merit in Sanskrit; and the Sūtra of Wondrous Contemplation Meditation in Tibetan — several dozen scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 元起朔方，固已崇尚釋教。

translations.literal: The Yuan arose in the northern frontier and from the outset already venerated Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: From its origins on the northern steppe the Yuan dynasty had already embraced Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 及得西域，世祖以其地廣而險遠，民獷而好鬥，思有以因其俗而柔其人，乃郡縣土番之地，設官分職，而領之於帝師。

translations.literal: When they obtained the Western Regions, the Founder of the Dynasty, because that land was broad yet perilous and distant, and the people fierce and fond of fighting, thought to have some means of following their customs to soften their people; thereupon in the Tibetan lands they established prefectures and counties, set officials and divided duties, and placed them under the leadership of the Imperial Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: After conquering the western territories Kublai saw that the region was vast, remote, and perilous, its inhabitants fierce and warlike. Seeking to govern them through their own customs, he organized Tibetan lands into administrative units under officials appointed by the Imperial Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 乃立宣政院，其為使位居第二者，必以僧為之，出帝師所辟舉，而總其政於內外者，帥臣以下，亦必僧俗並用，而軍民通攝。

translations.literal: Thereupon they established the Xuanzheng Commission; for its commissioner, whoever held the second rank must be a monk, nominated by the Imperial Preceptor, while those overseeing affairs within and without — commanders and below — also had to employ monks and laity together, with military and civil jointly administered.
translations.idiomatic: The court established the Xuanzheng Commission, whose second-ranking commissioner was always a monk nominated by the Imperial Preceptor. Regional commanders and their subordinates combined monastic and lay officials, exercising authority over both military and civilian affairs.

sentences.zh: 於是帝師之命，與詔敕並行於西土。

translations.literal: Thus the commands of the Imperial Preceptor proceeded in parallel with imperial edicts throughout the western lands.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the Imperial Preceptor's orders carried equal weight with imperial edicts throughout the western territories.

sentences.zh: 百年之間，朝廷所以敬禮而尊信之者，無所不用其至。

translations.literal: Within a hundred years, in all the court's showing of respect and honoring trust toward him, there was nothing to which they did not bring their utmost.
translations.idiomatic: For a century the court spared no gesture of reverence and trust toward the Imperial Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 雖帝后妃主，皆因受戒而為之膜拜。

translations.literal: Even empresses and imperial consorts all, because of receiving precepts, performed prostration before him.
translations.idiomatic: Even empresses and imperial consorts received ordination from him and bowed before him in worship.

sentences.zh: 正衙朝會，百官班列，而帝師亦或專席於坐隅。

translations.literal: At regular court assemblies in the main hall, the hundred officials stood in ranks, yet the Imperial Preceptor also sometimes had a special seat in a corner of the seating.
translations.idiomatic: At formal court audiences, while officials stood in their ranks, the Imperial Preceptor sometimes occupied a seat of honor apart from them.

sentences.zh: 且每帝即位之始，降詔褒護，必敕章佩監絡珠為字以賜，蓋其重之如此。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the beginning of each emperor's accession, edicts of praise and protection were sent down, invariably ordering the Directorate of Seals and Credentials to inscribe pearl characters to bestow — such was the weight they placed upon him.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of every new reign the court issued edicts of praise and protection, invariably ordering the Directorate of Seals to inscribe his titles in pearls for presentation — such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 其未至而迎之，則中書大臣馳驛累百騎以往，所過供億送迎。

translations.literal: Before his arrival, to welcome him, a chief minister of the Central Secretariat would gallop post-horses with a cumulative hundred riders to go forth; wherever he passed, provisions and escort were furnished.
translations.idiomatic: To welcome him before his arrival, a chief minister of the Central Secretariat would ride out with a hundred mounted escorts, and every post station along the route would supply provisions and attendants.

sentences.zh: 比至京師，則敕大府假法駕半仗，以為前導，詔省、台、院官以及百司庶府，並服銀鼠質孫。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, the Grand Provisionery was ordered to lend half the imperial regalia as vanguard; officials of the Secretariat, Censorate, and Court, and the hundred offices and various bureaus all wore silver-rat zhisun.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the capital the Grand Provisionery lent half the imperial procession as his escort, and officials of the Secretariat, Censorate, Court, and all government offices wore silver-rat fur robes in his honor.

sentences.zh: 用每歲二月八日迎佛，威儀往迓，且命禮部尚書、郎中專督迎接。

translations.literal: Using the eighth day of the second month each year to welcome the Buddha, with full ceremonial retinue going to meet him, and additionally ordering the Minister of Rites and a director to supervise the reception exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Each year on the eighth day of the second month the court welcomed the Buddha with full ceremonial escort, the Minister of Rites and a director being specially assigned to oversee the reception.

sentences.zh: 及其卒而歸葬舍利，又命百官出郭祭餞。

translations.literal: When he died and his relics were returned for burial, the hundred officials were again ordered to go beyond the walls to offer sacrificial farewell.
translations.idiomatic: When he died and his relics were escorted home for burial, all officials were ordered to go beyond the city walls to offer farewell sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 大德九年，專遣平章政事鐵木兒乘​​傳護送，賻金五百兩、銀千兩、幣帛萬匹、鈔三千錠。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dade, a special dispatch sent the Grand Councillor Temür traveling post-horses to escort and protect; funeral gifts were five hundred taels of gold, a thousand taels of silver, ten thousand bolts of silks, and three thousand ingots of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Dade era the court specially dispatched Grand Councillor Temür by relay post to escort the remains, with funeral gifts of five hundred taels of gold, a thousand taels of silver, ten thousand bolts of silk, and three thousand ingots of paper money.

sentences.zh: 皇慶二年，加至賻金五千兩、銀一萬五千兩、錦綺雜彩共一萬七千匹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangqing, it was increased to funeral gifts of five thousand taels of gold, fifteen thousand taels of silver, and brocades and miscellaneous silks totaling seventeen thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Huangqing era the standard was raised to five thousand taels of gold, fifteen thousand taels of silver, and seventeen thousand bolts of brocade and colored silk.

sentences.zh: 雖其昆弟子姓之往來，有司亦供億無乏。

translations.literal: Even for the coming and going of his disciples, nephews, and clansmen, the responsible offices also furnished provisions without shortage.
translations.idiomatic: Even the comings and goings of his disciples, nephews, and kinsmen were supplied with provisions at public expense.

sentences.zh: 泰定間，以帝師弟公哥亦思監將至，詔中書持羊酒郊勞；

translations.literal: During Taiding, because the Imperial Preceptor's younger brother Kun dga' ye shes rgyal mtshan was about to arrive, an edict ordered the Central Secretariat to hold sheep and wine for suburban welcome;
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiding era, when the Imperial Preceptor's younger brother Kun-dga' ye-shes was expected, the Central Secretariat was ordered to greet him in the suburbs with sheep and wine;

sentences.zh: 而其兄瑣南藏卜遂尚公主，封白蘭王，賜金印，給圓符。

translations.literal: while his elder brother Sog bzang po then married an imperial princess, was enfeoffed as Prince of Bailan, bestowed a gold seal, and given round tallies.
translations.idiomatic: while his elder brother Sog-bzang-po married an imperial princess, was enfeoffed as Prince of Bailan, and received a gold seal and round tallies of authority.

sentences.zh: 其弟子之號司空、司徒、國公，佩金玉印章者，前後相望。

translations.literal: His disciples bearing the titles Minister of Works, Minister of Education, and State Duke, wearing gold and jade seals — one after another in sight.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples who held titles such as Minister of Works, Minister of Education, and State Duke, wearing gold and jade seals, formed an unbroken succession.

sentences.zh: 為其徒者，怙勢恣睢，日新月盛，氣焰熏灼，延於四方，為害不可勝言。

translations.literal: Those who were his followers, relying on power and acting wantonly, daily grew in new abundance; their aura scorched and extended to the four directions — the harm cannot be fully told.
translations.idiomatic: His followers abused their power with growing arrogance day by day. Their influence blazed across the realm, and the harm they inflicted is beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 有楊璉真加者，世祖用為江南釋教總統，發掘故宋趙氏諸陵之在錢唐、紹興者及其大臣塚墓凡一百一所；

translations.literal: There was Yang Lianzhenjia, whom the Founder of the Dynasty employed as Jiangnan Buddhist President; he excavated the former Song Zhao clan tombs located at Qiantang and Shaoxing and their great ministers' graves — one hundred and one places in all;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Lianzhenjia, whom Kublai appointed president of the Buddhist clergy in Jiangnan, desecrated one hundred and one tombs — including the Song imperial Zhao tombs at Qiantang and Shaoxing and the graves of Song ministers;

sentences.zh: 戕殺平民四人；

translations.literal: slaughtered four common civilians;
translations.idiomatic: murdered four commoners;

sentences.zh: 受人獻美女寶物無算；

translations.literal: received from people offerings of beautiful women and treasures beyond counting;
translations.idiomatic: accepted countless bribes of beautiful women and precious goods;

sentences.zh: 且攘奪盜取財物，計金一千七百兩、銀六千八百兩、玉帶九、玉器大小百一十有一、雜寶貝百五十有二、大珠五十兩、鈔一十一萬六千二百錠、田二萬三千畝；

translations.literal: moreover plundered and stole property, totaling: gold one thousand seven hundred taels, silver six thousand eight hundred taels, nine jade belts, large and small jade vessels one hundred and eleven, miscellaneous treasures and shells one hundred and fifty-two, large pearls fifty taels, paper money one hundred eleven thousand six hundred ingots, fields twenty-three thousand mu;
translations.idiomatic: and plundered property totaling one thousand seven hundred taels of gold, six thousand eight hundred taels of silver, nine jade belts, one hundred eleven jade vessels large and small, one hundred fifty-two miscellaneous gems and shells, fifty taels of large pearls, one hundred eleven thousand six hundred ingots of paper money, and twenty-three thousand mu of farmland;

sentences.zh: 私庇平民不輸公賦者二萬三千戶。

translations.literal: privately sheltered twenty-three thousand households of common people who did not pay public taxes.
translations.idiomatic: and sheltered twenty-three thousand households who evaded public taxes.

sentences.zh: 他所藏匿未露者不論也。

translations.literal: What he concealed elsewhere and did not expose is not reckoned.
translations.idiomatic: To say nothing of what he concealed and was never discovered.

sentences.zh: 又至大元年，上都開元寺西僧強市民薪，民訴諸留守李璧。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the first year of Zhida, at Shangdu's Kaiyuan Temple a Western monk forcibly seized firewood from townspeople; the people complained to the resident commissioner Li Bi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhida era, at Shangdu's Kaiyuan Temple a Tibetan monk forcibly seized firewood from townspeople, who appealed to the resident commissioner Li Bi.

sentences.zh: 璧方詢問其由，僧已率其黨持白梃突入公府，隔案引璧發，捽諸地，捶撲交下，拽之以歸，閉諸空室，久乃得脫，奔訴於朝，遇赦以免。

translations.literal: Bi was just inquiring into the cause when the monk already led his faction holding white cudgels to burst into the government office, pulled Bi by the hair across the desk, threw him to the ground, beatings raining down, dragged him back, shut him in an empty room — only after long could he escape, ran to complain at court, and met an amnesty and was spared punishment.
translations.idiomatic: While Bi was still investigating, the monk led his followers armed with clubs into the government office, seized Bi by the hair across his desk, threw him to the ground, and beat him severely. They dragged him away and locked him in a room; he eventually escaped and appealed to the capital, but received amnesty before punishment could be imposed.

sentences.zh: 二年，復有僧龔柯等十八人，與諸王合兒八剌妃忽禿赤的斤爭道，拉妃墮車毆之，且有犯上等語，事聞，詔釋不問。

translations.literal: In the second year, again there were eighteen monks including Gong'e and others who disputed the road with the consort Hutuchidijin of Prince Herbala; they pulled the consort from her carriage and beat her, and moreover had words offending superiors — when the matter was reported, an edict released them without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The following year eighteen monks led by Gong'e disputed the right of way with the consort Hutuchidijin of Prince Her-bala, pulled her from her carriage, beat her, and uttered words of lese-majesty. When the matter was reported, an edict ordered them released without punishment.

sentences.zh: 而宣政院臣方奏取旨：凡民毆西僧者，截其手；

translations.literal: Meanwhile members of the Xuanzheng Commission were just memorializing to obtain instructions: whenever commoners beat Western monks, cut off their hands;
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Xuanzheng Commission was petitioning for an edict: any commoner who struck a Tibetan monk was to have his hand cut off;

sentences.zh: 詈之者，斷其舌。

translations.literal: who reviled them, cut off their tongues.
translations.idiomatic: anyone who cursed them was to have his tongue cut out.

sentences.zh: 時仁宗居東宮，聞之，亟奏寢其令。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Renzong resided in the Eastern Palace; hearing of it, he urgently memorialized to suspend the order.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Renzong, residing in the Eastern Palace, heard of this and immediately memorialized to have the order withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 泰定二年，西台御史李昌言：「嘗經平涼府、靜、會、定西等州，見西番僧佩金字圓符，絡繹道途，馳騎累百，傳舍至不能容，則假館民舍，因迫逐男子，姦污女婦。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiding, Western Terrace Censor Li Chang said: "I once passed through Pingliang prefecture, Jing, Hui, Dingxi, and other prefectures, and saw Western monks wearing gold-letter round tallies, crowding the roads in succession, galloping in companies of a hundred; when relay stations could no longer hold them, they borrowed lodging in commoners' houses, thereby driving off men and defiling women."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Taiding era, Censor Li Chang of the Western Terrace memorialized: "I have traveled through Pingliang prefecture and the prefectures of Jing, Hui, and Dingxi, and seen Tibetan monks wearing gold-letter round tallies thronging the highways in companies of a hundred mounted riders. When relay stations could not accommodate them, they commandeered private homes, driving off the men and assaulting the women."

sentences.zh: 奉元一路，自正月至七月，往返者百八十五次，用馬至八百四十餘匹，較之諸王、行省之使，十多六七。

translations.literal: On the Fengyuan circuit alone, from the first month to the seventh, there were one hundred eighty-five round trips, using horses reaching more than eight hundred forty — compared with envoys of princes and branch secretariats, more than six or seven tenths greater.
translations.idiomatic: On the Fengyuan circuit alone, from the first to the seventh month, monks made one hundred eighty-five round trips using more than eight hundred forty horses — sixty to seventy percent more than the missions of princes and provincial administrations.

sentences.zh: 驛戶無所控訴，台察莫得誰何。

translations.literal: Relay households had nowhere to appeal; the censorate could obtain no means to deal with them.
translations.idiomatic: Relay households had no recourse for complaint, and the censorate was powerless to intervene.

sentences.zh: 且國家之制圓符，本為邊防警報之虞，僧人何事而輒佩之？

translations.literal: Moreover, the state's regulation on round tallies was originally for border defense and alarm contingencies — what business have monks to wear them at will?
translations.idiomatic: Round tallies were originally issued for border defense and military emergencies. By what right do monks wear them at will?

sentences.zh: 乞更正僧人給驛法，且令台憲得以糾察。

translations.literal: I beg to correct the law on supplying relay service to monks, and moreover order that the censorate and surveillance commissioners may investigate and correct.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the regulations governing monks' use of relay service be revised, and that censorial officials be empowered to investigate and punish abuses."

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: No response was given.

sentences.zh: 必蘭納識里之誅也，有司籍之，得其人畜土田、金銀貨貝錢幣、邸舍、書畫器玩，以及婦人七寶裝具，價直巨萬萬云。

translations.literal: When Vimuktisri was executed, the responsible offices registered his property and obtained his livestock, fields, gold, silver, goods, money, mansions, books, paintings, and curios, as well as women's seven-treasure fittings — worth tens of millions, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: When Vimuktisri was executed, officials inventoried his property: livestock, farmland, gold and silver, goods, currency, mansions, books, paintings, curios, and women's jewelry fittings — said to be worth tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 若歲時祝釐禱祠之常，號稱好事者，其目尤不一。

translations.literal: As for the regular annual prayers and sacrifices, and those styled "doing good deeds," their categories are especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The regular annual prayers and merit-making ceremonies, and those called "good works," were especially numerous in kind.

sentences.zh: 有曰鎮雷阿藍納四，華言慶贊也。

translations.literal: There is one called Zhenlei Alanasi, which in Chinese means "celebratory praise."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Zhenlei Alanasi, meaning in Chinese "celebratory praise."

sentences.zh: 有曰亦思滿藍，華言藥師壇也。

translations.literal: There is one called Yisimanlan, which in Chinese means "Medicine Master altar."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Yisimanlan, meaning "Medicine Master altar."

sentences.zh: 有曰搠思串卜，華言護城也。

translations.literal: There is one called Suosichuanbu, which in Chinese means "protecting the city."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Suosichuanbu, meaning "city protection."

sentences.zh: 有曰朵兒禪，華言大施食也。

translations.literal: There is one called Duo'erchan, which in Chinese means "great food offering."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Duo'erchan, meaning "great food offering."

sentences.zh: 有曰朵兒只列朵四，華言美妙金剛回遮施食也。

translations.literal: There is one called Duo'erzhilieduosi, which in Chinese means "wondrous Vajra turning-back food offering."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Duo'erzhilieduosi, meaning "wondrous Vajra turning-back food offering."

sentences.zh: 有曰察兒哥朵四，華言回遮也。

translations.literal: There is one called Cha'ergeduosi, which in Chinese means "turning back."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Cha'ergeduosi, meaning "turning back."

sentences.zh: 有曰籠哥兒，華言風輪也。

translations.literal: There is one called Longge'er, which in Chinese means "wind wheel."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Longge'er, meaning "wind wheel."

sentences.zh: 有曰喒朵四，華言作施食也。

translations.literal: There is one called Zaduosi, which in Chinese means "performing food offering."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Zaduosi, meaning "performing food offering."

sentences.zh: 月曰出朵兒，華言出水濟六道也。

translations.literal: Monthly there is Chuduo'er, which in Chinese means "releasing water to aid the six paths."
translations.idiomatic: Monthly there was Chuduo'er, meaning "releasing water to aid the six paths of rebirth."

sentences.zh: 有曰黨剌朵四，華言回遮施食也。

translations.literal: There is one called Dangladuosi, which in Chinese means "turning-back food offering."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Dangladuosi, meaning "turning-back food offering."

sentences.zh: 有曰典朵兒，華言常川施食也。

translations.literal: There is one called Dianduo'er, which in Chinese means "perpetual food offering."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Dianduo'er, meaning "perpetual food offering."

sentences.zh: 有曰坐靜，有曰魯朝，華言獅子吼道場也。

translations.literal: There is seated meditation; there is Luchao, which in Chinese means "Lion's Roar dharma arena."
translations.idiomatic: There was seated meditation; there was Luchao, meaning "Lion's Roar dharma arena."

sentences.zh: 有曰黑牙蠻答哥，華言黑獄帝主也。

translations.literal: There is one called Heiyamandage, which in Chinese means "Black Hell Lord."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Heiyamandage, meaning "Lord of the Black Hell."

sentences.zh: 有曰搠思江朵兒麻，華言護法神施食也。

translations.literal: There is one called Suosijiangduo'erma, which in Chinese means "dharma-protecting deity food offering."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Suosijiangduo'erma, meaning "dharma-protecting deity food offering."

sentences.zh: 有曰赤思古林搠，華言自受主戒也。

translations.literal: There is one called Chisigulinsuo, which in Chinese means "self-receiving main precepts."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Chisigulinsuo, meaning "self-receiving main precepts."

sentences.zh: 有曰鎮雷坐靜，有曰吃剌察坐靜，華言秘密坐靜也。

translations.literal: There is Zhenlei seated meditation; there is Chilacha seated meditation, which in Chinese means "secret seated meditation."
translations.idiomatic: There was Zhenlei seated meditation and Chilacha seated meditation, meaning "secret seated meditation."

sentences.zh: 有曰斟惹，華言文殊菩薩也。

translations.literal: There is one called Zhenre, which in Chinese means "Manjushri Bodhisattva."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Zhenre, meaning "Manjushri Bodhisattva."

sentences.zh: 有曰古林朵四，華言至尊大黑神回遮施食也。

translations.literal: There is one called Gulingduosi, which in Chinese means "Supreme Great Black Deity turning-back food offering."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Gulingduosi, meaning "Supreme Great Black Deity turning-back food offering."

sentences.zh: 有曰歇白咱剌，華言大喜樂也。

translations.literal: There is one called Xiebaizhala, which in Chinese means "great bliss."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Xiebaizhala, meaning "great bliss."

sentences.zh: 有曰必思禪，華言無量壽也。

translations.literal: There is one called Bisichan, which in Chinese means "Amitābha."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Bisichan, meaning "Amitābha."

sentences.zh: 有曰睹思哥兒​​，華言白傘蓋咒也。

translations.literal: There is one called Dusige'er, which in Chinese means "White Parasol mantra."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Dusige'er, meaning "White Parasol mantra."

sentences.zh: 有曰收札沙剌，華言《五護陀羅尼經》也。

translations.literal: There is one called Shouzhashala, which in Chinese means the "Five Protective Dhāraṇī Sūtra."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Shouzhashala, meaning the Five Protective Dhāraṇī Sūtra.

sentences.zh: 有曰阿昔答撒哈昔裡，華言《八千頌般若經》也。

translations.literal: There is one called Axidasahaxili, which in Chinese means the "Eight Thousand-Verse Prajñā Sūtra."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Axidasahaxili, meaning the Eight Thousand-Verse Prajñā Sūtra.

sentences.zh: 有曰撒思納屯，華言《大理天神咒》也。

translations.literal: There is one called Sasinatun, which in Chinese means the "Great Divine Mantra of the Li Kingdom."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Sasinatun, meaning the Great Divine Mantra of the Li Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 有曰闊兒魯弗卜屯，華言《大輪金剛咒》也。

translations.literal: There is one called Kuo'erlufubutun, which in Chinese means the "Great Wheel Vajra Mantra."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Kuo'erlufubutun, meaning the Great Wheel Vajra Mantra.

sentences.zh: 有曰且八迷屯，華言《無量壽經》也。

translations.literal: There is one called Qiebamitun, which in Chinese means the "Amitāyus Sūtra."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Qiebamitun, meaning the Amitāyus Sūtra.

sentences.zh: 有曰亦思羅八，華言《最勝王經》也。

translations.literal: There is one called Yisiluoba, which in Chinese means the "Sūtra of the King of Ultimate Victory."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Yisiluoba, meaning the Sūtra of the King of Ultimate Victory.

sentences.zh: 有曰撒思納屯，華言《護神咒》也。

translations.literal: There is one called Sasinatun, which in Chinese means the "Protective Spirit Mantra."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Sasinatun, meaning the Protective Spirit Mantra.

sentences.zh: 有曰南佔屯，華言《懷相金剛》也。

translations.literal: There is one called Nazhantun, which in Chinese means the "Embodied Vajra of Devotion."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Nazhantun, meaning the Embodied Vajra of Devotion.

sentences.zh: 有曰卜魯八，華言咒法也。

translations.literal: There is one called Buluba, which in Chinese means "mantra methods."
translations.idiomatic: One was called Buluba, meaning "mantra methods."

sentences.zh: 又有作擦擦者，以泥作小浮屠也。

translations.literal: There is also the making of tsatsa — using clay to make small stūpas.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the making of tsatsa, small clay stūpas.

sentences.zh: 又有作答兒剛者。

translations.literal: There is also the making of dagan'gang.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the making of dagan'gang.

sentences.zh: 其作答兒剛者，或一所二所以至七所；

translations.literal: Those who make dagan'gang may do one site, two sites, up to seven sites;
translations.idiomatic: Dagan'gang could be built at one, two, or up to seven sites;

sentences.zh: 作擦擦者，或十萬二十萬以至三十萬。

translations.literal: those who make tsatsa may make one hundred thousand, two hundred thousand, up to three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: tsatsa could be made in quantities of one hundred thousand, two hundred thousand, or up to three hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 又嘗造浮屠二百一十有六，實以七寶珠玉，半置海畔，半置水中，以鎮海災。

translations.literal: They also once built two hundred sixteen stūpas, filled with the seven treasures and gems, half placed on the seashore and half in the water, to quell sea disasters.
translations.idiomatic: They also once built two hundred sixteen stūpas filled with the seven treasures, half placed on the seashore and half in the water to quell maritime disasters.

sentences.zh: 延祐四年，宣徽使會每歲內廷佛事所供，其費以斤數者，用面四十三萬九千五百、油七萬九千、酥二萬一千八百七十、蜜二萬七千三百。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanyou, the Xuanwei Commissioner tallied what the inner court Buddhist affairs supplied each year, measured in jin: flour four hundred thirty-nine thousand five hundred, oil seventy-nine thousand, butter twenty-one thousand eight hundred seventy, honey twenty-seven thousand three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Yanyou era the Xuanwei Commissioner tallied annual supplies for inner-court Buddhist affairs by weight: four hundred thirty-nine thousand five hundred jin of flour, seventy-nine thousand of oil, twenty-one thousand eight hundred seventy of butter, and twenty-seven thousand three hundred of honey.

sentences.zh: 自至元三十年間，醮祠佛事之目，僅百有二。

translations.literal: From the thirtieth year of Zhiyuan onward, the categories of Daoist and Buddhist ceremonies numbered barely one hundred and two.
translations.idiomatic: From the thirtieth year of the Zhiyuan era onward, the categories of Buddhist and Daoist ceremonies numbered barely one hundred and two.

sentences.zh: 大德七年，再立功德司，遂增至五百有餘。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dade, the Merit Commissioner's office was re-established, and they increased to more than five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Dade era the Merit Commissioner's office was re-established, and the number rose to more than five hundred.

sentences.zh: 僧徒貪利無已，營結近侍，欺昧奏請，布施莽齋，所需非一，歲費千萬，較之大德，不知幾倍。

translations.literal: Monks, greedy for profit without end, cultivated connections with palace attendants, deceived and obscured in memorializing, bestowing alms and vegetarian feasts — what was required was not one kind; annual expenditure reached tens of millions, compared with Dade, not knowing how many times greater.
translations.idiomatic: Monks, insatiably greedy for profit, cultivated connections with palace attendants and secured deceptive memorials for alms and vegetarian feasts. Annual expenditure reached tens of millions — many times the cost under the Dade era.

sentences.zh: 又每歲必因好事奏釋輕重囚徒，以為福利​​，雖大臣如阿里，閫帥如別沙兒等，莫不假是以逭其誅。

translations.literal: Moreover each year they inevitably memorialized on good works to release prisoners of lighter or heavier guilt as merit — even great ministers such as Ali and frontier commanders such as Biesha'er mostly borrowed this to escape their punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Every year they memorialized for the release of prisoners, light and heavy alike, as a meritorious act — even great ministers such as Ali and frontier commanders such as Biesha'er often used this to escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 宣政院參議李良弼，受賕鬻官，直以帝師之言縱之。

translations.literal: Xuanzheng Commission Participating Councillor Li Liangbi, accepting bribes to sell offices, simply on the Imperial Preceptor's word released them.
translations.idiomatic: Participating Councillor Li Liangbi of the Xuanzheng Commission accepted bribes to sell offices and released offenders simply on the Imperial Preceptor's word.

sentences.zh: 其餘殺人之盜，作姦之徒，夤緣倖免者多。

translations.literal: The rest — murdering robbers, adulterous offenders — who curried favor to escape were many.
translations.idiomatic: Murderers, thieves, and adulterers who curried favor to escape justice were legion.

sentences.zh: 至或取空名宣敕以為布施，而任其人，可謂濫矣。

translations.literal: To the point of sometimes taking empty-title edicts of bestowal and entrusting persons at will — one may say it was excessive.
translations.idiomatic: They even took blank edicts of bestowal and filled in names at will — a degree of license beyond all bounds.

sentences.zh: 凡此皆有關乎一代之治體者，故今備著焉。

translations.literal: All these bear on the governing institutions of an age; therefore they are fully set forth here.
translations.idiomatic: All of this bore on the governing institutions of the dynasty; therefore it is fully recorded here.

sentences.zh: 若夫天下寺院之領於內外宣政院，曰禪，曰教，曰律，則固各守其業，惟所謂白雲宗、白蓮宗者，亦或頗通姦利云。

translations.literal: As for temples throughout the realm under the inner and outer Xuanzheng Commission — Chan, Teaching, and Vinaya — they each kept to their profession; only the so-called White Cloud and White Lotus sects also somewhat mingled with illicit profit.
translations.idiomatic: Temples throughout the realm under the Xuanzheng Commission — whether Chan, Teaching, or Vinaya schools — each kept to its own discipline; only the so-called White Cloud and White Lotus sects were also said to traffic somewhat in illicit gain.

sentences.zh: 丘處機，登州棲霞人，自號長春子。

translations.literal: Qiu Chuji was a man of Qixia in Deng prefecture; he styled himself Master Changchun.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Chuji was a native of Qixia in Deng prefecture and styled himself Master Changchun.

sentences.zh: 兒時，有相者謂其異日當為神仙宗伯。

translations.literal: In childhood, a physiognomist told him that another day he would become patriarch of the immortals.
translations.idiomatic: As a child a physiognomist told him he would one day become patriarch of the immortals.

sentences.zh: 年十九，為全真學於寧海之崑崙山，與馬鈺、譚處端、劉處玄、王處一、郝大通、孫不二同師重陽王真人。

translations.literal: At age nineteen he studied Quanzhen teachings on Mount Kunlun in Ninghai, together with Ma Yu, Tan Chuduan, Liu Chuxuan, Wang Chuyi, Hao Datong, and Sun Bu'er — all disciples of Wang Chongyang the Perfected One.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he studied Quanzhen Daoism on Mount Kunlun in Ninghai, together with Ma Yu, Tan Chuduan, Liu Chuxuan, Wang Chuyi, Hao Datong, and Sun Bu'er, all disciples of Wang Chongyang the Perfected One.

sentences.zh: 重陽一見處機，大器之。

translations.literal: Chongyang, upon first meeting Chuji, greatly valued his capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Upon first meeting Chuji, Chongyang recognized his exceptional talent.

sentences.zh: 金、宋之季，俱遣使來召，不赴。

translations.literal: In the twilight of Jin and Song, both sent envoys to summon him; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the declining years of the Jin and Song dynasties, both courts sent envoys to summon him, but he refused to go.

sentences.zh: 歲己卯，太祖自乃蠻命近臣札八兒、劉仲祿持詔求之。

translations.literal: In the year jimao, the Founder of the Dynasty, from the Naiman, ordered his close attendant Zhaba'er and Liu Zhonglu to hold an edict seeking him.
translations.idiomatic: In the jimao year the Founder, then campaigning against the Naiman, ordered his close attendant Zhaba'er and Liu Zhonglu to bring an edict summoning him.

sentences.zh: 處機一日忽語其徒，使促裝，曰：「天使來召我，我當往。

translations.literal: Chuji one day suddenly told his disciples to hurry their packing, saying: "Envoys have come to summon me; I must go."
translations.idiomatic: One day Chuji suddenly told his disciples to pack quickly, saying, "Envoys have come to summon me. I must go."

sentences.zh: 」翌日，二人者至，處機乃與弟子十有八人同往見焉。

translations.literal: " The next day the two arrived; Chuji then went with eighteen disciples together to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the two envoys arrived, and Chuji set out with eighteen disciples to meet them.

sentences.zh: 明年，宿留山北，先馳表謝，拳拳以止殺為勸。

translations.literal: The following year, lodging north of the mountains, he first sent a memorial of thanks, earnestly urging cessation of killing.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, while lodging north of the mountains, he sent a memorial of thanks earnestly urging the emperor to stop killing.

sentences.zh: 又明年，趣使再至，乃發撫州，經數十國，為地萬有餘里。

translations.literal: The year after, envoys urging him came again; he then set out from Fuzhou, passing through dozens of states — a journey of more than ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The year after, envoys came again to urge him onward. He set out from Fuzhou and traveled through dozens of states — a journey of more than ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 蓋蹀血戰場，避寇叛域，絕糧沙漠，自崑崙歷四載而始達雪山。

translations.literal: He tramped through bloody battlefields, skirted rebel territories, and ran out of food in the desert; from Kunlun it took four years before he reached Snow Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed blood-soaked battlefields, skirted rebel-held territories, and nearly starved in the desert; from Kunlun it took four years to reach the Snow Mountain.

sentences.zh: 常馬行深雪中，馬上舉策試之，未及積雪之半。

translations.literal: Often riding through deep snow, he would raise his whip from horseback to test it — yet not reach half the depth of the accumulated snow.
translations.idiomatic: Often riding through snow so deep that when he raised his whip from horseback it did not reach halfway to the surface.

sentences.zh: 既見，太祖大悅，賜食、設廬帳甚飭。

translations.literal: Upon meeting [the Founder], the Founder was greatly pleased, bestowed food, and set up a tent lodging with great care.
translations.idiomatic: When he met the Founder, the emperor was greatly pleased, bestowed food upon him, and set up a tent with great care.

sentences.zh: 太祖時方西征，日事攻戰，處機每言欲一天下者，必在乎不嗜殺人。

translations.literal: The Founder was then on western campaigns, daily engaged in attack and battle; Chuji each time said that whoever wishes to unify the realm must lie in not being fond of killing people.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder was then on western campaigns, fighting daily. Chuji repeatedly said that whoever wishes to unify the realm must begin by ceasing to delight in killing.

sentences.zh: 及問為治之方，則對以敬天愛民為本。

translations.literal: When asked the method of governing, he replied that revering Heaven and loving the people were the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: When asked how to govern, he answered that revering Heaven and loving the people were the foundation.

sentences.zh: 問長生久視之道，則告以清心寡欲為要。

translations.literal: Asked about the Way of long life and long vision, he told them that purifying the mind and reducing desires were essential.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about the path to longevity, he said that purifying the mind and reducing desires were essential.

sentences.zh: 太祖深契其言，曰：「天錫仙翁，以寤朕志。

translations.literal: The Founder deeply matched his words, saying: "Heaven bestows the Immortal Elder to awaken Our will."
translations.idiomatic: The Founder was deeply moved and said, "Heaven has sent the Immortal Elder to awaken my will."

sentences.zh: 」命左右書之，且以訓諸子焉。

translations.literal: " He ordered attendants to write it down, and moreover used it to instruct his sons.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered attendants to write this down and used it to instruct his sons.

sentences.zh: 於是錫之虎符，副以璽書，不斥其名，惟曰「神仙」。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bestowed on him a tiger tally, with imperial writ as supplement, not reproaching his name but only calling him "Immortal."
translations.idiomatic: He then bestowed on him a tiger tally and imperial writ, addressing him only as "Immortal" without using his personal name.

sentences.zh: 一日雷震，太祖以問，處機對曰：「雷，天威也。

translations.literal: One day thunder crashed; the Founder asked about it, and Chuji replied: "Thunder is Heaven's majesty."
translations.idiomatic: One day thunder crashed. The Founder asked its meaning, and Chuji replied, "Thunder is Heaven's majesty."

sentences.zh: 人罪莫大於不孝，不孝則不順乎天，故天威震動以警之。

translations.literal: Among human crimes none is greater than unfilial conduct; unfilial conduct then is not compliant with Heaven — therefore Heaven's majesty shakes to warn them.
translations.idiomatic: No human crime is greater than unfilial piety. Unfilial conduct defies Heaven, and so Heaven shakes with thunder to warn the people.

sentences.zh: 似聞境內不孝者多，陛下宜明天威，以導有眾。

translations.literal: "It seems I have heard that within the borders unfilial persons are many; Your Majesty should clarify Heaven's majesty to guide the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: I hear that unfilial conduct is widespread within the realm. Your Majesty should make Heaven's majesty clear to guide the people."

sentences.zh: 」太祖從之。

translations.literal: " The Founder followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 歲癸未，太祖大獵於東山，馬踣，處機請曰：「天道好生，陛下春秋高，數畋獵，非宜。

translations.literal: In the year guiwei, the Founder made a great hunt on the Eastern Mountain; his horse stumbled, and Chuji requested: "Heaven's Way loves life; Your Majesty's years are high, and frequent hunting is not fitting."
translations.idiomatic: In the guiwei year the Founder held a great hunt on the Eastern Mountain. When his horse stumbled, Chuji said, "Heaven's Way cherishes life. Your Majesty is advanced in years, and frequent hunting is unfitting."

sentences.zh: 」太祖為罷獵者久之。

translations.literal: " The Founder for this reason ceased hunting for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder accordingly refrained from hunting for a long time.

sentences.zh: 時國兵踐蹂中原，河南、北尤甚，民罹俘戮，無所逃命。

translations.literal: At that time the state's armies trampled the Central Plain; Henan and Hebei suffered especially — the people met capture and slaughter with nowhere to flee for their lives.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the armies trampled the Central Plain, and Henan and Hebei suffered most grievously. The people faced capture and slaughter with nowhere to flee.

sentences.zh: 處機還燕，使其徒持牒招求於戰伐之餘，由是為人奴者得復為良，與濱死而得更生者，毋慮二三萬人。

translations.literal: Chuji returned to Yan and had his disciples hold documents to recruit and seek out survivors in the aftermath of warfare — thereby those who had become others' slaves could again become good commoners, and those on the brink of death who obtained renewed life numbered no less than twenty or thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Chuji returned to Yan and sent his disciples out with documents to seek survivors in the war-ravaged lands. Those who had been enslaved were restored to free status, and those snatched from death numbered no fewer than twenty or thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 中州人至今稱道之。

translations.literal: People of the Central Plain to this day speak of it with praise.
translations.idiomatic: People of the Central Plain still speak of this with praise.

sentences.zh: 歲乙酉，熒惑犯尾，其占在燕，處機禱之，果退舍。

translations.literal: In the year yiyou, the Sparkling Deluder invaded the Tail constellation; its omen lay in Yan, and Chuji prayed — it indeed retreated.
translations.idiomatic: In the yiyou year the Sparkling Deluder invaded the Tail constellation, whose omen concerned the Yan region. Chuji prayed, and the star indeed retreated.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，又為旱禱，期以三日雨，當名瑞應，已而亦驗。

translations.literal: In dinghai, he again prayed for drought; he set a term of three days' rain as an auspicious response — afterward it was also verified.
translations.idiomatic: In the dinghai year he prayed for rain during a drought, promising three days' rain as an auspicious sign — and it came to pass.

sentences.zh: 有旨改賜宮名曰長春，且遣使勞問，制若曰：「朕常念神仙，神仙毋忘朕也。

translations.literal: An order changed and bestowed on his palace the name Changchun, and moreover sent envoys to comfort and inquire, writing: "We constantly think of the Immortal; let the Immortal not forget Us."
translations.idiomatic: An edict renamed his monastery Changchun and sent envoys to inquire after him, writing, "We constantly think of the Immortal; let the Immortal not forget us."

sentences.zh: 」六月，浴於東溪，越二日，天大雷雨，太液池岸北水入東湖，聲聞數里，魚鱉盡去，池遂涸，而北口高岸亦崩，處機歎曰：「山其摧乎，池其涸乎，吾將與之俱乎！

translations.literal: " In the sixth month, bathing in the Eastern Stream — two days later heaven sent great wind and thunder; the northern waters of the Great Liquid Pool entered the Eastern Lake, the sound heard for several li, fish and turtles all departed, the pool thereby dried up, and the high northern bank also collapsed. Chuji sighed: "Will the mountain be destroyed? Will the pool dry up? Shall I perish together with them!"
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, while bathing in the Eastern Stream, two days later a great thunderstorm struck. The northern waters of the Great Liquid Pool flooded into the Eastern Lake with a roar heard for several li. Fish and turtles fled, the pool dried up, and the high northern bank collapsed. Chuji sighed, "Will the mountain fall? Will the pool dry up? Must I perish with them?"

sentences.zh: 」遂卒，年八十。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he died, age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 其徒尹志平等世奉璽書襲掌其教，至大間加賜金印。

translations.literal: His disciple Yin Zhiping and others for generations received imperial writ and inherited his teaching; during the Zhida period a gold seal was additionally bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: His disciple Yin Zhiping and successors for generations received imperial writ and inherited his teaching; during the Zhida era a gold seal was additionally bestowed.

sentences.zh: 處機之四傳有曰祁志誠者，居雲州金閣山，道譽甚著。

translations.literal: Among Chuji's fourth-generation transmitters was one named Qi Zhicheng, who dwelt on Mount Jinge in Yun prefecture; his Way's reputation was very prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Among Chuji's fourth-generation disciples was Qi Zhicheng, who lived on Mount Jinge in Yun prefecture and enjoyed a renowned reputation.

sentences.zh: 丞相安童嘗過而問之，志誠告以修身治世之要。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor An Tong once passed by and questioned him; Zhicheng told him the essentials of cultivating the self and ordering the age.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor An Tong once visited him, and Zhicheng taught him the essentials of self-cultivation and governance.

sentences.zh: 安童感其言，故其相世祖也，以清靜忠厚為主。

translations.literal: An Tong was moved by his words; therefore when he served as the Founder's of the Dynasty's chancellor, he took purity, tranquility, and loyalty as his main principles.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his words, when An Tong served as Kublai's chancellor he made purity, tranquility, and loyalty his guiding principles.

sentences.zh: 及罷還第，退然若無與於世者，人以為有得於志誠之言。

translations.literal: When dismissed and returned to his residence, he was retiring as if he had no part in worldly affairs — people thought he had gained something from Zhicheng's words.
translations.idiomatic: When dismissed and returned home, he lived in retirement as if removed from worldly affairs. People believed he had gained wisdom from Zhicheng's teaching.

sentences.zh: 其後安童復被召入相，辭，不可，遂往決於志誠。

translations.literal: Afterward An Tong was again summoned to enter the chancellorship; he declined but could not refuse, and thereupon went to decide at Zhicheng's.
translations.idiomatic: Later An Tong was summoned back to the chancellorship. He wished to decline but could not refuse, and went to consult Zhicheng.

sentences.zh: 志誠曰：「昔與子同列者何人？

translations.literal: Zhicheng said: "In former days, who were your colleagues in the same rank?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng asked, "In former days, who were your colleagues of equal rank?"

sentences.zh: 今同列者何人？

translations.literal: "Who are your colleagues in the same rank now?"
translations.idiomatic: "And who are your colleagues of equal rank now?"

sentences.zh: 」安童悟，入見世祖，辭曰：「臣昔為宰相，年尚少，幸不失陛下事者，丞佐皆臣所師友。

translations.literal: " An Tong understood, entered to see the Founder of the Dynasty, and declined, saying: "Your subject formerly served as chancellor when still young, and was fortunate not to fail Your Majesty's affairs because my assisting colleagues were all my teachers and friends."
translations.idiomatic: An Tong understood. He went to see Kublai and declined, saying, "When I formerly served as chancellor I was still young, and was fortunate not to fail Your Majesty's affairs because my colleagues were all my teachers and friends."

sentences.zh: 今事臣者，皆進與臣俱，則臣之為政能有加於前乎！

translations.literal: "Those who now serve me are all promoted together with me — how can my governance surpass what it was before!"
translations.idiomatic: Those who now serve under me were all promoted together with me. How can my governance surpass what it was before?"

sentences.zh: 」世祖曰：「誰為卿言是？

translations.literal: " The Founder of the Dynasty said: "Who told you this is right?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Who told you this is correct?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「祁真人。

translations.literal: " He replied: "The Perfected One Qi."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Master Qi the Perfected One."

sentences.zh: 」世祖嘆異者久之。

translations.literal: " The Founder of the Dynasty sighed in wonder for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai marveled at this for a long time.

sentences.zh: 正一天師者，始自漢張​​道陵，其後四代曰盛，來居信之龍虎山。

translations.literal: The Zhengyi Heavenly Master began with Zhang Daoling of Han; afterward four generations called Sheng came to dwell at Dragon-Tiger Mountain in Xin.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhengyi Heavenly Master lineage began with Zhang Daoling of the Han dynasty. After four generations the family surname became Sheng, and they settled at Dragon-Tiger Mountain in Xin prefecture.

sentences.zh: 相傳至三十六代宗演，當至元十三年，世祖已平江南，遣使召之。

translations.literal: The transmission reached the thirty-sixth generation, Zongyan; in the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan the Founder of the Dynasty had already pacified Jiangnan and sent envoys to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: The line descended to the thirty-sixth generation, Zhang Zongyan. In the thirteenth year of the Zhiyuan era, after Kublai had pacified the south, he sent envoys to summon him.

sentences.zh: 至則命廷臣郊勞，待以客禮。

translations.literal: When he arrived, court ministers were ordered to welcome him in the suburbs and he was received with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his arrival the court ordered officials to greet him in the suburbs and received him with the honors due a guest.

sentences.zh: 及見，語之曰：「昔歲己未，朕次鄂渚，嘗令王一清往訪卿父，卿父使報朕曰：後二十年天下當混一。

translations.literal: When he was received, [the emperor] said to him: "In former years jiwei, We were stationed at Ezhu and once ordered Wang Yiqing to visit your father; your father sent word to Us saying: within twenty years the realm will be unified.
translations.idiomatic: When they met, the emperor said, "In the jiwei year I was stationed at Ezhou and sent Wang Yiqing to visit your father. Your father sent word that within twenty years the realm would be unified.

sentences.zh: 神仙之言驗於今矣。

translations.literal: The immortal's words are verified today.
translations.idiomatic: The immortal's prophecy has been fulfilled today.

sentences.zh: 」因命坐，錫宴，特賜玉芙蓉冠、組金無縫服，命主領江南道教，仍賜銀印。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was ordered to be seated, granted a feast, specially bestowed a jade hibiscus crown and seamless gold-thread robe, ordered to head Jiangnan Daoism, and still given a silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: " He was seated and feasted, presented with a jade hibiscus crown and seamless gold-thread robe, appointed to head Daoism in Jiangnan, and given a silver seal.

sentences.zh: 十八年、二十五年再入覲。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth and twenty-fifth years he again entered court audience.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court in the eighteenth and twenty-fifth years.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗命取其祖天師所傳玉印、寶劍觀之，語侍臣曰：「朝代更易已不知其幾，而天師劍印傳子若孫尚至今日，其果有神明之相矣乎！

translations.literal: The Founder of the Dynasty once ordered the jade seal and precious sword transmitted by his ancestor the Heavenly Master brought for viewing, and told attending ministers: "Dynasties have changed — who knows how many times — yet the Heavenly Master's sword and seal transmitted son to grandson still reach today; do they truly have the aspect of divine intelligence!
translations.idiomatic: Kublai once ordered the jade seal and precious sword handed down from the founding Heavenly Master brought for inspection and told his ministers, "Dynasties have changed countless times, yet the Heavenly Master's sword and seal have passed from father to son down to this day. Can there truly be divine power in them?

sentences.zh: 」嗟嘆久之。

translations.literal: " He sighed in admiration for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed in wonder for a long time.

sentences.zh: 二十九年卒，子與棣嗣，為三十七代，襲掌江南道教。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died; his son Yudi succeeded as the thirty-seventh generation, inheriting control of Jiangnan Daoism.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-ninth year. His son Yudi succeeded him as the thirty-seventh generation and inherited leadership of Jiangnan Daoism.

sentences.zh: 三十一年入覲，卒於京師。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he entered court audience and died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He came to court in the thirty-first year and died in the capital.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，弟與材嗣，為三十八代，襲掌道教。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen, his younger brother Yucai succeeded as the thirty-eighth generation, inheriting control of Daoism.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yuanzhen era his younger brother Yucai succeeded as the thirty-eighth generation and inherited leadership of the Daoist clergy.

sentences.zh: 時潮囓鹽官、海鹽兩州，為患特甚，與材以術治之。

translations.literal: At that time the tide gnawed at Yan'guan and Haiyan prefectures, the harm being especially severe; Yucai treated it with his arts.
translations.idiomatic: At that time tidal flooding ravaged Yan'guan and Haiyan prefectures with particular severity, and Yucai treated it with ritual methods.

sentences.zh: 一夕大雷電以震，明日見有物魚首龜形者磔於水裔，潮患遂息。

translations.literal: One night great thunder and lightning shook; the next day they saw a creature with a fish head and tortoise body dismembered on the water's edge, and the tidal harm ceased.
translations.idiomatic: One night a great thunderstorm struck. The next day a creature with a fish's head and tortoise's body was found dismembered on the shore, and the tidal flooding ceased.

sentences.zh: 大德五年，召見於上都幄殿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dade he was summoned for audience in the curtained hall at Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Dade era he was summoned to audience at Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 八年，授正一教主，主領三山符籙。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Zhengyi Teaching Lord, heading the talismans of the Three Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Lord of the Zhengyi Teaching and placed in charge of the talismans of the Three Mountains.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，來覲，特授金紫光祿大夫，封留國公，錫金印。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong ascended, he came to audience, was specially appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Purple, enfeoffed as Duke of Liu, and bestowed a gold seal.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Yucai came to court and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Purple, enfeoffed as Duke of Liu, and given a gold seal.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，特賜寶冠、組織文金之服。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong ascended, he was specially bestowed a precious crown and gold-thread patterned robe.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, he received a precious crown and gold-thread ceremonial robe.

sentences.zh: 延祐三年卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanyou he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of the Yanyou era.
