sentences.zh: 四年，子嗣成嗣，為三十九代，襲領江南道教，主領三山符籙如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year his son Sicheng succeeded as the thirty-ninth generation, inheriting leadership of Jiangnan Daoism and heading the Three Mountains talismans as before.
translations.idiomatic: The following year his son Sicheng succeeded as the thirty-ninth generation, inheriting leadership of Jiangnan Daoism and the Three Mountains talismans as before.

sentences.zh: 其徒張留孫者，字師漢，信州貴溪人。

translations.literal: His disciple Zhang Liusun, styled Shihan, was a man of Guixi in Xin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Among his disciples was Zhang Liusun, styled Shihan, a native of Guixi in Xin prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少時入龍虎山為道士，有道人相之曰：「神仙宰相也。

translations.literal: In youth he entered Dragon-Tiger Mountain as a Daoist priest; a Daoist physiognomized him, saying: "Immortal and chancellor both.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he became a Daoist priest on Dragon-Tiger Mountain. A fellow priest read his features and declared, "He will be both immortal and chancellor.

sentences.zh: 」至元十三年，從天師張宗演入朝，世祖與語，稱旨，遂留侍闕下。

translations.literal: " In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan he followed Heavenly Master Zhang Zongyan to court; the Founder of the Dynasty spoke with him, found his words pleasing, and thereupon retained him to attend below the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: " In the thirteenth year of the Zhiyuan era he accompanied Heavenly Master Zhang Zongyan to court. Kublai spoke with him, was pleased, and retained him at the palace.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗親祠幄殿，皇太子侍。

translations.literal: The Founder of the Dynasty once personally sacrificed at the curtained hall, with the Crown Prince in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai once performed sacrifice at the curtained hall with the crown prince in attendance.

sentences.zh: 忽風雨暴至，眾駭懼，留孫禱之立止。

translations.literal: Suddenly wind and rain came violently; the multitude were terrified, but Liusun prayed and it immediately stopped.
translations.idiomatic: A violent storm suddenly broke. Everyone was terrified, but Liusun prayed and it stopped at once.

sentences.zh: 又嘗次日月山，昭睿順聖皇后得疾危甚，亟召留孫請禱。

translations.literal: He also once stopped at Sun-Moon Mountain when Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng fell gravely ill; she urgently summoned Liusun to pray.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, while encamped at Sun-Moon Mountain, Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng fell gravely ill and urgently summoned Liusun to pray for her.

sentences.zh: 既而後夢有硃衣長髯，從甲士，導硃輦白獸行草間者。

translations.literal: Afterward the empress dreamed of one in red robes with long beard, followed by armored soldiers, guiding a red carriage and white beast walking through grass.
translations.idiomatic: The empress then dreamed of a man in red robes with a long beard, followed by armored soldiers guiding a red carriage drawn by a white beast through the grass.

sentences.zh: 覺而異之，以問留孫，對曰：「甲士導輦獸者，臣所佩法籙中將吏也；

translations.literal: Awakening, she found it strange and asked Liusun; he replied: "The armored soldiers guiding the carriage and beast are the generals and officers in the talisman registers I wear;
translations.idiomatic: Awakening, she found it strange and asked Liusun. He replied, "The armored soldiers guiding the carriage and beast are the generals and officers in the talisman registers I wear.

sentences.zh: 硃衣長髯者，漢祖天師也；

translations.literal: the one in red robes with long beard is the founding Heavenly Master of Han;
translations.idiomatic: The man in red robes with a long beard is the founding Heavenly Master of the Han.

sentences.zh: 行草間者，春時也。

translations.literal: walking through grass signifies the season of spring.
translations.idiomatic: Walking through the grass signifies the season of spring.

sentences.zh: 殿下之疾，其及春而瘳乎！

translations.literal: Your Highness's illness — will it recover by spring!
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness's illness should recover by spring!

sentences.zh: 」後命取所事畫像以進，視之果夢中所見者。

translations.literal: " Later she ordered the portrait he venerated brought forth; viewing it, it was indeed what she had seen in the dream.
translations.idiomatic: She later ordered the portrait he venerated brought forth — and it was indeed what she had seen in the dream.

sentences.zh: 帝后大悅，即命留孫為天師，留孫固辭不敢當，乃號之上卿，命尚方鑄寶劍以賜，建崇真宮於兩京，俾留孫居之，專掌祠事。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress were greatly pleased and immediately ordered Liusun made Heavenly Master; Liusun firmly declined and dared not accept, so he was styled Supreme Minister instead; the Imperial Workshop was ordered to cast a precious sword to bestow; Chongzhen Palaces were built in both capitals for Liusun to dwell in, exclusively overseeing sacrificial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress were delighted and offered to make Liusun Heavenly Master. He firmly declined, and was instead styled Supreme Minister. The Imperial Workshop cast a precious sword for him, and Chongzhen Palaces were built in both capitals for him to reside in and oversee sacrificial affairs.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授玄教宗師，錫銀印。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Xuanjiao Patriarch and bestowed a silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching and given a silver seal.

sentences.zh: 又特任其父信州路治中，尋复升江東道同知宣慰司事。

translations.literal: His father was also specially appointed administrative vice-commissioner of Xin prefecture circuit, and soon afterward promoted to associate commissioner of the Jiangdong Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: His father was specially appointed administrative vice-commissioner of Xin circuit and soon promoted to associate commissioner of the Jiangdong Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 是時天下大定，世祖思與民休息，留孫待詔尚方，因論黃老治道貴清淨、聖人在宥天下之旨，深契主衷。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was greatly settled; the Founder of the Dynasty wished to let the people rest. Liusun awaited edicts at the Imperial Workshop and, discussing how the Yellow Emperor and Laozi's way of governance values purity and tranquility and how the sage leaves the realm in repose, deeply matched the sovereign's heart.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was now largely pacified, and Kublai wished to let the people rest. Liusun attended at court and expounded how the governance of Huang-Lao values purity and tranquility and how the sage leaves the realm in repose — teachings that deeply matched the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 及將以完澤為相，命留孫筮之，得《同人》之《豫》，留孫進曰：「'《同人》，柔得位而應乎乾'，君臣之合也；

translations.literal: When about to appoint Wanze as chancellor, he ordered Liusun to divine by milfoil; he obtained Tongren changing to Yu. Liusun advanced and said: "'Tongren — the yielding obtains position and responds to Qian' — the union of ruler and minister;
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai was about to appoint Wanze as chancellor, he ordered Liusun to divine. The hexagram was Tongren changing to Yu. Liusun said, "'Tongren: the yielding obtains position and responds to Qian' — this signifies the union of ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: '《豫》，利建侯'，命相之事也。

translations.literal: 'Yu — favorable to establishing lords' — the matter of appointing a chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: 'Yu: favorable to establishing lords' — this concerns appointing a chancellor.

sentences.zh: 何吉如之，願陛下勿疑。

translations.literal: What could be more auspicious? I beg Your Majesty not to doubt.
translations.idiomatic: What could be more auspicious? I beg Your Majesty not to hesitate.

sentences.zh: 」及拜完澤，天下果以為得賢相。

translations.literal: " When Wanze was appointed, the realm indeed regarded it as obtaining a worthy chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanze was appointed, the realm indeed regarded it as the choice of a worthy chancellor.

sentences.zh: 大德中，加號玄教大宗師，同知集賢院道教事，且追封其三代皆魏國公，官階品俱第一。

translations.literal: During Dade, he was given the added title Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching, Associate Commissioner of the Hall of Worthies for Daoist affairs, and his three generations were posthumously enfeoffed all as Dukes of Wei, official ranks all of the first grade.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dade era he received the added title Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching and was made associate commissioner of the Hall of Worthies for Daoist affairs. His three generations of ancestors were posthumously enfeoffed as Dukes of Wei with first-grade ranks.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，召見，賜坐，升大真人，知集賢院，位大學士上。

translations.literal: When Wuzong ascended, he was summoned for audience, granted a seat, promoted to Great Perfected One, made director of the Hall of Worthies, ranking above Grand Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong took the throne, Liusun was summoned, granted a seat, promoted to Great Perfected One, made director of the Hall of Worthies, and ranked above the grand academicians.

sentences.zh: 尋又加特進。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was additionally made Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the additional rank of Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 進講老子推明謙讓之道。

translations.literal: He advanced to lecture on Laozi, extending and clarifying the Way of humility and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured on Laozi, expounding the way of humility and yielding.

sentences.zh: 及仁宗即位，猶恆誦其言，且諭近臣曰：「累朝舊德，僅餘張上卿爾。

translations.literal: When Renzong ascended, he still constantly recited his words, and moreover instructed close ministers: "The accumulated virtue of successive reigns — only Supreme Minister Zhang remains.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took the throne he still often quoted Liusun's teachings and told his close ministers, "Of the accumulated virtue of successive reigns, only Supreme Minister Zhang remains.

sentences.zh: 」進開府儀同三司，加號輔成贊化保運玄教大宗師，刻玉為玄教大宗師印以賜。

translations.literal: " He was advanced to Opening the Mansion, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, with the added title Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching, Assisting Completion, Praising Transformation, Protecting the Fortune; a jade seal of Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching was carved and bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Honorary Three Excellencies of the First Rank and given the added title Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching, Assisting Completion and Praising Transformation. A jade seal was carved and bestowed upon him.

sentences.zh: 至治元年十二月卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Zhizhi he died, age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month of the first year of the Zhizhi era at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 天曆元年，追贈道祖神德真君。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianli he was posthumously granted the title Perfected Lord of the Dao Ancestor's Divine Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tianli era he was posthumously honored as Perfected Lord of the Dao Ancestor's Divine Virtue.

sentences.zh: 其徒吳全節嗣。

translations.literal: His disciple Wu Quanjie succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His disciple Wu Quanjie succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 全節字成季，饒州安仁人。

translations.literal: Quanjie, styled Chengji, was a man of Anren in Rao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Quanjie, styled Chengji, was a native of Anren in Rao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 年十三學道於龍虎山。

translations.literal: At age thirteen he studied the Way on Dragon-Tiger Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he began studying the Way on Dragon-Tiger Mountain.

sentences.zh: 至元二十四年至京師，從留孫見世祖。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Zhiyuan he reached the capital and, following Liusun, met the Founder of the Dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of the Zhiyuan era he came to the capital and, accompanying Liusun, met Kublai.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，成宗至自朔方，召見，賜古雕玉蟠螭環一，敕每歲侍從行幸，所司給廬帳、車馬、衣服、廩餼，著為令。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, when Chengzong returned from the northern frontier, he was summoned for audience and bestowed one ancient carved jade coiled-dragon ring; he was ordered each year to attend the emperor on tours, with the responsible offices supplying tents, horses, clothing, and provisions — established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year, when Chengzong returned from the north, Quanjie was summoned and given an ancient carved jade ring with coiled dragons. He was ordered to accompany the emperor on annual tours, with tents, horses, clothing, and provisions supplied by regulation.

sentences.zh: 大德十一年，授玄教嗣師，錫銀印，視二品。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dade he was appointed Successor Master of the Xuan Teaching, bestowed a silver seal, treated as second rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Dade era he was appointed Successor Master of the Xuan Teaching, given a silver seal, and treated as second rank.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，賜七寶金冠、織金文之服。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida he was bestowed a seven-treasure gold crown and gold-thread patterned robe.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhida era he received a seven-treasure gold crown and gold-thread ceremonial robe.

sentences.zh: 三年，贈其祖昭文館大學士，封其父司徒、饒國公，母饒國太夫人，名其所居之鄉曰榮祿，裡曰具慶。

translations.literal: In the third year his grandfather was posthumously granted Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall; his father was enfeoffed as Minister of Education and Duke of Rao; his mother as Grand Lady of Rao; his home village was named Ronglu and his hamlet Jiqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year his grandfather was posthumously made Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall; his father was enfeoffed as Minister of Education and Duke of Rao; his mother as Grand Lady of Rao; his home village was named Ronglu and his hamlet Jiqing.

sentences.zh: 至治元年，留孫卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi, Liusun died.
translations.idiomatic: Liusun died in the first year of the Zhizhi era.

sentences.zh: 二年，制授特進、上卿、玄教大宗師、崇文弘道玄德真人、總攝江淮荊襄等處道教、知集賢院道教事，玉印一、銀印二並授之。

translations.literal: In the second year, by regulation he was appointed Special Advancement, Supreme Minister, Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching, Perfected One of Honoring Culture and Expanding the Way with Mysterious Virtue, General Overseer of Daoism in Jianghuai, Jingxiang, and other regions, and Director of the Hall of Worthies for Daoist affairs — one jade seal and two silver seals were all bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Special Advancement, Supreme Minister, Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching, and Perfected One of Honoring Culture and Expanding the Way, placed in charge of Daoism throughout Jianghuai, Jingxiang, and other regions, and made director of the Hall of Worthies for Daoist affairs, with one jade seal and two silver seals.

sentences.zh: 全節嘗代祀岳瀆還，成宗問曰：「卿所過郡縣，有善治民者乎？

translations.literal: Quanjie once returned from substituting in sacrifice to the mountains and rivers; Chengzong asked: "Among the prefectures and counties you passed, are there any who govern the people well?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, returning from substituting in sacrifice to the mountains and rivers, Chengzong asked him, "Among the prefectures and counties you passed through, did you find any who govern the people well?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣過洛陽，太守盧摯平易無為，而民以安靖。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Your subject passed Luoyang; the prefect Lu Zhi is plain and easy, practicing non-action, yet the people are thereby peaceful and settled."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I passed through Luoyang. The prefect Lu Zhi governs with plain ease and non-action, yet the people are peaceful and settled."

sentences.zh: 」成宗曰：「吾憶其人。

translations.literal: " Chengzong said: "We recall that man."
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong said, "I remember that man."

sentences.zh: 」即日召拜集賢學士。

translations.literal: " That same day he was summoned and appointed Academician of the Hall of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Lu Zhi was summoned and appointed Academician of the Hall of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 成宗崩，仁宗至自懷孟，有狂士以危言訐翰林學士閻复者，事叵測。

translations.literal: When Chengzong died, Renzong arrived from Huai-Meng; a madman used alarming words to denounce Hanlin Academician Yan Fu — the affair was hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong died and Renzong arrived from Huai-Meng, a madman denounced Hanlin Academician Yan Fu with alarming words, and the affair's outcome was uncertain.

sentences.zh: 全節力為言於李孟，孟以聞，仁宗意解，復告老而去。

translations.literal: Quanjie strenuously spoke on his behalf to Li Meng; Meng reported it, Renzong's mind was eased, and Fu requested retirement and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Quanjie spoke earnestly on Yan Fu's behalf to Li Meng, who reported it to Renzong. The emperor's anger eased, and Yan Fu retired and departed.

sentences.zh: 當時以為朝廷得敬大臣體，而不以口語傷賢者，全節蓋有力焉。

translations.literal: At the time it was thought the court had obtained the proper respect for great ministers and did not harm the worthy through loose words — Quanjie had strength in this.
translations.idiomatic: At the time people credited the court with showing proper respect for great ministers and not harming the worthy on loose charges — in which Quanjie had played a significant part.

sentences.zh: 全節雅好結士大夫，無所不傾其交，長者尤見親而敬，推轂善類，唯恐不盡其力。

translations.literal: Quanjie elegantly loved forming ties with scholar-officials, sparing nothing to pour out his friendship; elders he especially treated with intimacy and respect, promoting the good, fearing only that he had not exhausted his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Quanjie delighted in befriending scholar-officials and gave his friendship unstintingly. He was especially intimate with and respectful toward elders, promoting worthy men and exhausting every effort on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 至於振窮周急，又未嘗以恩怨異其心，當時以為頗有俠氣云。

translations.literal: As for relieving the poor and aiding the urgent, he also never altered his heart because of favor or resentment; at the time he was thought to possess quite a chivalrous spirit.
translations.idiomatic: In relieving the poor and aiding those in distress he never let personal favor or resentment sway him. At the time he was regarded as possessing a chivalrous spirit.

sentences.zh: 全節卒，年八十有二，其徒夏文泳嗣。

translations.literal: Quanjie died at age eighty-two; his disciple Xia Wenyong succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Quanjie died at the age of eighty-two. His disciple Xia Wenyong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 真大道教者，始自金季，道士劉德仁之所立也。

translations.literal: The True Great Way teaching began in the Jin season; it was established by the Daoist priest Liu Deren.
translations.idiomatic: The True Great Way teaching was founded during the Jin dynasty by the Daoist priest Liu Deren.

sentences.zh: 其教以苦節危行為要，而不妄取於人、不苟侈於己者也。

translations.literal: Its teaching takes bitter discipline and perilous conduct as essential, not taking from others recklessly nor being extravagant with oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Its teaching emphasized austere discipline and rigorous conduct, taking nothing recklessly from others and indulging nothing in oneself.

sentences.zh: 五傳而至酈希成，居燕城天寶宮，見知憲宗，始名其教曰真大道，授希成太玄真人，領教事，內出冠服以賜；

translations.literal: After five transmissions it reached Li Xicheng, who dwelt at the Tianbao Palace in Yan city; he came to the notice of Emperor Xianzong, who first named the teaching the True Great Way, appointed Xicheng Perfected One of the Great Mystery, placed him in charge of teaching affairs, and issued from within court caps and robes to bestow;
translations.idiomatic: After five generations the line reached Li Xicheng, who lived at the Tianbao Palace in Yan. Emperor Xianzong took notice of him, named the teaching the True Great Way, appointed Xicheng Perfected One of the Great Mystery to head it, and bestowed court caps and robes;

sentences.zh: 仍給紫衣三十襲，賜其從者。

translations.literal: still giving thirty suits of purple robes to bestow on his followers.
translations.idiomatic: and gave thirty purple robes for his followers.

sentences.zh: 至元五年，世祖命其徒孫德福統轄諸路真大道，錫銅章。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhiyuan, the Founder of the Dynasty ordered his disciple Sun Defu to oversee the True Great Way in all circuits and bestowed a bronze seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Zhiyuan era Kublai ordered his disciple Sun Defu to oversee the True Great Way in all circuits and bestowed a bronze seal.

sentences.zh: 二十年，改賜銀印二。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, two silver seals were changed and bestowed instead.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he received two silver seals in place of the bronze one.

sentences.zh: 又三傳而至張清志，其教益盛，授演教大宗師、凝神衝妙玄應真人。

translations.literal: After three more transmissions it reached Zhang Qingzhi; the teaching grew still more prosperous; he was appointed Great Patriarch of the Expounding Teaching, Perfected One of Concentrating Spirit, Piercing Mystery, and Mysterious Response.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations later the line reached Zhang Qingzhi, under whom the teaching flourished further. He was appointed Great Patriarch of the Expounding Teaching and Perfected One of Concentrating Spirit and Piercing Mystery.

sentences.zh: 清志事親孝，尤耐辛苦，制行堅峻。

translations.literal: Qingzhi was filial in serving his parents, especially enduring hardship; his regulated conduct was stern and severe.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi was filial toward his parents, exceptionally enduring of hardship, and sternly disciplined in conduct.

sentences.zh: 東海珠、牢山舊多虎，清志往結茅居之，虎皆避徙，然頗為人害。

translations.literal: East of the sea at Zhuhai and Mount Lao there were formerly many tigers; Qingzhi went and built a thatched dwelling to live there — the tigers all avoided and moved away, yet they still harmed people considerably.
translations.idiomatic: East of the sea at Zhuhai and Mount Lao tigers were once numerous. Qingzhi built a thatched hut and lived there; the tigers all fled, yet they still harmed people elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 清志曰：「是吾奪其所也！

translations.literal: Qingzhi said: "This is because I seized their dwelling place!"
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said, "I have seized their dwelling place!

sentences.zh: 」遂去之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he left.
translations.idiomatic: So he departed.

sentences.zh: 後居臨汾，地大震，城郭邑屋摧壓，死者不可勝計，獨清誌所居裂為二，無少損焉。

translations.literal: Later he dwelt at Linfen; a great earthquake struck — city walls, towns, and houses were crushed; the dead could not be counted — only Qingzhi's dwelling split in two without the slightest damage.
translations.idiomatic: Later he lived at Linfen. A great earthquake struck, crushing cities and towns beyond count. Only Qingzhi's dwelling split in two without the slightest damage.

sentences.zh: 乃遍巡木石間，聽呻吟聲，救活者甚眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went everywhere among timbers and stones, listening for groaning sounds — those he saved alive were very many.
translations.idiomatic: He searched everywhere among the rubble, listening for groans, and saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 朝廷重其名，給驛致之掌教事。

translations.literal: The court valued his reputation and sent relay horses to bring him to head teaching affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court valued his reputation and sent relay horses to bring him to the capital to head the teaching.

sentences.zh: 清志舍傳徒步至京師，深居簡出，人或不識其面。

translations.literal: Qingzhi abandoned the relay posts and walked on foot to the capital, dwelling deeply and going out rarely — some did not know his face.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi abandoned the relay posts and walked to the capital on foot. He lived in seclusion and rarely went out, so that some did not know his face.

sentences.zh: 貴人達官來見，率告病，伏臥內不起。

translations.literal: When nobles and high officials came to see him, he invariably pleaded illness and lay prostrate within, not rising.
translations.idiomatic: When nobles and high officials came to visit, he invariably pleaded illness and would not rise from his bed.

sentences.zh: 至於道德縉紳先生，則納屣杖屨求見，不以為難。

translations.literal: As for cultivated gentlemen of virtue and girdled sashes, he would put on shoes and take staff to seek them out, not considering it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: But for cultivated gentlemen of learning and virtue he would put on his shoes and take his staff to visit them without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 時人高其風，至畫為圖以相傳焉。

translations.literal: People of the time admired his bearing, even painting pictures to pass down.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries admired his character, and paintings of him were passed down.

sentences.zh: 太一教者，始金天眷中道士蕭抱珍，傳太一三元法​​籙之術，因名其教曰太一。

translations.literal: The Supreme Unity teaching began with the Daoist priest Xiao Baozhen in the Jintianjuan period of Jin, transmitting the arts of the Supreme Unity Three Origins talismans — therefore naming the teaching Supreme Unity.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Unity teaching was founded by the Daoist priest Xiao Baozhen during the Jintianjuan era of the Jin dynasty, who transmitted the arts of the Supreme Unity Three Origins talismans and named the teaching accordingly.

sentences.zh: 四傳而至蕭輔道。

translations.literal: After four transmissions it reached Xiao Fudao.
translations.idiomatic: After four generations the line reached Xiao Fudao.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潛邸聞其名，命史天澤召至和林，賜對稱旨，留居宮邸。

translations.literal: The Founder of the Dynasty, while at his princely residence, heard his name and ordered Shi Tianze to summon him to Helin; an imperial audience found his words pleasing, and he was retained to dwell at the palace residence.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai, while still at his princely residence, heard of him and ordered Shi Tianze to summon him to Helin. An audience found his words pleasing, and he was retained at the palace.

sentences.zh: 以老，請授弟子李居壽掌其教事。

translations.literal: Because of age, he requested that his disciple Li Jushou take charge of teaching affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On account of age he asked that his disciple Li Jushou take charge of the teaching.

sentences.zh: 至元十一年，建太一宮於兩京，命居壽居之，領祠事，且禋祀六丁，以繼太保劉秉忠之術。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan, Supreme Unity Palaces were built in both capitals; Jushou was ordered to dwell there, heading sacrificial affairs, and moreover performing suburban sacrifice to the Six Ding — continuing the arts of Grand Guardian Liu Bingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Zhiyuan era Supreme Unity Palaces were built in both capitals. Jushou was placed in residence to head sacrificial affairs and perform suburban rites to the Six Ding, continuing the arts of Grand Guardian Liu Bingzhong.

sentences.zh: 十三年，賜太一掌教宗師印。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the seal of Supreme Unity Patriarch in Charge of Teaching was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he received the seal of Supreme Unity Patriarch in Charge of Teaching.

sentences.zh: 十六年十月辛丑，月直元辰，敕居壽祠醮，奏赤章於天，凡五晝夜。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, xinchou day, of the sixteenth year, when the moon was directly on the primordial spirit, Jushou was ordered to perform temple sacrifice and deliverance rites, presenting red memorials to Heaven — in all five days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day of the tenth month of the sixteenth year, when the moon aligned with the primordial spirit, Jushou was ordered to perform temple rites and present red memorials to Heaven for five days and nights.

sentences.zh: 事畢，居壽請間曰：「皇太子春秋鼎盛，宜參預國政。

translations.literal: When the affair was concluded, Jushou requested a private audience and said: "The Crown Prince is in the full vigor of spring and autumn; he ought to participate in state affairs."
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were concluded, Jushou requested a private audience and said, "The crown prince is in the prime of life and ought to participate in state affairs."

sentences.zh: 」且又因典瑞董文忠以為言，世祖喜曰：「行將及之。

translations.literal: " Moreover, through Court Regalia Officer Dong Wenzong he also spoke on this; the Founder of the Dynasty was pleased and said: "It will soon be carried out."
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke through Court Regalia Officer Dong Wenzong. Kublai was pleased and said, "It shall soon be done."

sentences.zh: 」其後詔太子參決朝政，庶事皆先啟後聞者，蓋居壽為之先也。

translations.literal: " Afterward an edict ordered the Crown Prince to participate in deciding court governance; for ordinary affairs all were first reported to him and then announced — Jushou was the one who initiated this.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter an edict ordered the crown prince to participate in deciding government affairs, with all routine matters reported to him first — Jushou had been the initiator of this.
